This file is always managed — it is refreshed with the bundle even when `../SKILL.md` has been customized.\n4|\n5|Shared protocol (environment, auth, idempotency, dry-run, polling, and error handling) lives in `../SKILL.md`.\n6|\n7|## Workflow Guidance\n8|\n9|Use this reference to collect structured public data for research, monitoring, lead preparation, and content analysis.\n10|\n11|### Match the business outcome\n12|\n13|| Outcome | Start with | Continue with |\n14|| --- | --- | --- |\n15|| Extract a site or document | `/v1/scrape/website` or `/v1/scrape/pdf` | Follow discovered pages only when the task needs them |\n16|| Research developers or software | `/v1/scrape/github/search` | GitHub repository, profile, issues, pulls, contents, or commits |\n17|| Research people, companies, or hiring | LinkedIn people, company, or jobs endpoints | LinkedIn profile or posts for deeper context |\n18|| Research creators and content | `/v1/scrape/youtube/search` | YouTube transcript, channel, or shorts |\n19|| Monitor conversations and audience response | X/Twitter, Reddit, or Instagram search/list endpoints | User, posts, replies, or comments |\n20|| Research advertising | `/v1/scrape/facebook/ads` | Go deep: competitor `pages` plus keyword queries, `activeStatus: \"all\"`, `maxItems` 100+ (see the Meta Ads recipe below) |\n21|| Find local businesses and places | `/v1/scrape/google/places` | Narrow by location and category; set `maxItems: 1` when looking up one specific business (much faster and cheaper) |\n22|\n23|### Recommended workflow\n24|\n25|1. Define the entities and fields the final output needs.\n26|2. Use the dedicated platform endpoint. Never replace it with open-web search.\n27|3. Discover identifiers first, then call detail endpoints only for relevant results.\n28|4. Size `maxItems` to the job, not to caution: on cheap per-item endpoints (Meta ads ~$0.003 per ad) request 100+, and continue with returned page tokens whenever the task needs more.\n29|5. Preserve source URLs and report missing, private, blocked, or partial data honestly.\n30|\n31|### Important constraints\n32|\n33|- Do not send a GitHub token or OAuth credential; DeepAPI handles GitHub authentication server-side and returns public resources only.\n34|- Website and PDF extraction requires public URLs. PDFs must have a readable text layer; image-only scans are not OCRed.\n35|- Bound large pages, documents, and transcripts with `maxChars` or `maxPages`. A `truncated: true` result reached that cap.\n36|- Continue pagination by returning `nextPageToken` unchanged as `pageToken` with the same filters. GitHub profile repository pagination additionally requires `includeRepos: true` and one username.\n37|\n38|### Meta Ads Library research recipe (`/v1/scrape/facebook/ads`)\n39|\n40|One call is not research. Ads cost ~$0.003 each, so depth costs cents while shallow results are worthless. For competitor or market research, fan out 3-5 calls and merge:\n41|\n42|- Run BOTH kinds of calls: `pages` for each competitor (returns everything an advertiser runs) and keyword `query` calls (keyword search only matches ad text, so it misses ads that never mention the term).\n43|- Always set `activeStatus: \"all\"` when researching: inactive ads reveal what an advertiser tested and stopped.\n44|- Vary keywords across calls: brand name, product name, tagline, category term.\n45|- When specific markets matter, query 2-3 key `country` codes in separate calls instead of relying on `ALL` — per-country searches can surface ads that `ALL` misses.\n46|- Request `maxItems` 100+ per call, then dedupe the merged results by ad `id`.\n47|\n48|### Go-deep recipes (high-value patterns)\n49|\n50|Per-item prices are cents or fractions of cents — depth is cheap and shallow results are worthless. Default patterns:\n51|\n52|- X/Twitter monitoring: run `sort: \"latest\"` AND `sort: \"top\"` plus 2-3 query phrasings, `maxItems` 100 each, then dedupe by tweet `id`. Enrich accounts in batches: `/v1/scrape/twitter/user` takes a handle list in one call, with optional `includeFollowers`/`includeFollowing` extraction.\n53|- Websites: pass a URL list to fetch many pages in one `/v1/scrape/website` call, or hand it one deep seed URL to crawl a whole docs/blog subtree — never fetch research pages one call at a time.\n54|- YouTube topics and creators: pull 25 search results or 30 channel videos, then transcript the top 5-10 relevant videos (~$0.02 each) with `/v1/scrape/youtube/transcript` — transcribing 10 videos costs ~$0.20.\n55|- LinkedIn lists: people search exists to build lists — ask for 50+ profiles per call, fan out titles x locations variants, then enrich the shortlist with `/v1/scrape/linkedin/profile`.\n56|\n57|### Reading a `/v1/scrape/website` response\n58|\n59|- `output` is an array of page objects. Each returned page carries the requested content (`markdown` and/or `text`, per `contentFormat`) and, when the origin reports it, a `url`. A page with no extractable content is dropped, so it never appears as a content-free result.\n60|- Per-page metadata fields are optional and present only when available: `title`, `description`, and `language` appear only when the page provides them; `truncated` and `totalChars` appear only on a page that hit the `maxChars` cap. Never assume a field exists; read defensively.\n61|- Follow the polling `next` (a `GET` of `/v1/requests/{requestId}`) whenever it is present, regardless of `status`. A billed run whose content is still settling returns `status: \"succeeded\"` with `output: null`, no `list`, and a polling `next`; poll it until it is absent before treating the result as complete. Do not stop polling just because `status` is no longer `running`, and never auto-follow a `POST` `next` (dry-run execution or paid pagination).\n62|- Read the `list.listState` signal beside `output` to tell an empty fetch from real pages: `results` (pages returned), `no_results` (the origin answered but returned nothing usable), or `source_blocked` (blocking was the dominant reason, for example an HTTP 401, 403, 407, 429, 451, or 503, or a login wall, captcha, rate limit, or access-denied notice). When the origin answers but returns nothing usable the fetch is free (`debitMicrousd: 0`) and `output` is an empty array.\n63|- A run can also end `status: \"failed\"` (for example a backend failure with no working fallback). A failed run is not a free empty success; surface the error instead of treating it as no content.\n64|\n65|### Find exact endpoint details\n66|\n67|- `GET /v1/capabilities` lists every available capability and slug.\n68|- `GET /v1/capabilities?capability=<slug>` returns the exact current schema, example, pricing, and availability for one endpoint.\n69|- `https://deepapi.co/docs/reference.md` is the complete agent-readable API reference.\n70|- `https://deepapi.co/docs/pricing.md` has current endpoint pricing.\n71|- `https://deepapi.co/openapi.json` is the machine-readable contract; `https://deepapi.co/llms.txt` indexes all public agent docs.\n72|", "total_lines": 71, "file_size": 6911, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Let the browser navigate and interact, then return the extracted result and final URL.\n16|4. Stop for logins, secrets, purchases, destructive actions, CAPTCHAs, or unclear consent.\n17|\n18|## Endpoint Details\n19|\n20|## Browser Task\n21|\n22|`POST /v1/browser/act`\n23|\n24|Run a goal-driven task in a real cloud browser and return its result.\n25|\n26|- Capability: `browser.act`\n27|- Scope: `browser:act`\n28|- Side effects: Performs real actions on public websites and debits credits when the task finishes.\n29|- Cost: Defaults to maxCostUsd 1.00. Finished tasks are billed per attempt, including tasks with isSuccess false. Failed and stopped tasks are free. Typical price: ~$0.10-$0.60 per task depending on steps.\n30|- Idempotency-Key: required\n31|- Polling: If the response carries a polling next action (a GET of /v1/requests/{requestId}), wait next.afterSecs and call it. Keep following that polling next while it is present, even when status is already succeeded (a settling run returns succeeded with output null and a polling next). The result is final when no polling next remains or status is failed. Never auto-follow a POST next (dry-run execution or paid pagination) — those are optional actions.\n32|\n33|Safety:\n34|- Public web only: tasks that need logins, credentials, account creation, CAPTCHA solving, or purchases are rejected.\n35|- Describe one concrete goal per task and set startUrl when you know the site.\n36|\n37|Request body schema:\n38|```json\n39|{\n40|  \"type\": \"object\",\n41|  \"required\": [\n42|    \"task\"\n43|  ],\n44|  \"properties\": {\n45|    \"task\": {\n46|      \"type\": \"string\",\n47|      \"maxLength\": 10000,\n48|      \"description\": \"What to do in the browser, in plain English. Defaults to 25, maximum 50.\"\n61|    },\n62|    \"outputSchema\": {\n63|      \"type\": \"object\",\n64|      \"additionalProperties\": true,\n65|      \"description\": \"Optional JSON Schema for a structured result.\"\n66|    },\n67|    \"allowedDomains\": {\n68|      \"type\": \"array\",\n69|      \"minItems\": 1,\n70|      \"maxItems\": 20,\n71|      \"items\": {\n72|        \"type\": \"string\"\n73|      },\n74|      \"description\": \"Optional allowed domains, like example.com or *.example.com.\"\n75|    },\n76|    \"maxCostUsd\": {\n77|      \"type\": \"string\",\n78|      \"pattern\": \"^\\\\d+(\\\\.\\\\d{1,6})?$\",\n79|      \"default\": \"1.00\",\n80|      \"description\": \"Optional customer spend cap in USD. Defaults to 1.00.\"\n81|    },\n82|    \"maxCostMicrousd\": {\n83|      \"type\": \"integer\",\n84|      \"minimum\": 1,\n85|      \"description\": \"Optional customer spend cap in USD micro-dollars.\"\n86|    },\n87|    \"dryRun\": {\n88|      \"type\": \"boolean\",\n89|      \"default\": false,\n90|      \"description\": \"Zero-spend preview: validate this request and return the exact credit hold it would place (status dry_run plus an estimate object) without reserving, charging, or running anything.\"\n91|    }\n92|  },\n93|  \"additionalProperties\": false\n94|}\n95|```\n96|\n97|Response schema:\n98|```json\n99|{\n100|  \"$ref\": \"#/components/schemas/PublicEnvelope\"\n101|}\n102|```\n103|\n104|Example request body:\n105|```json\n106|{\n107|  \"task\": \"Find the support email address on example.com.\",\n108|  \"startUrl\": \"https://example.com\",\n109|  \"maxCostUsd\": \"1.00\"\n110|}\n111|```\n112|", "total_lines": 111, "file_size": 4094, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}
